original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed using a VP-ITC microcalorimeter (MicroCal, Northampton, MA). The His6-tagged human recombinant PB1 bromodomain isoform 5 was expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)-R3-pRARE2 cells and purified as described previously.25 The protein was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05 mM TCEP, pH 7.5, and concentrated to 10–15 μM. The ligand was dissolved in DMSO and diluted in the same buffer to a final concentration of 1–2 mM. The protein was loaded into the sample cell (200 μL), and the ligand was loaded into the syringe (250 μL). The experiment was performed at 25 °C with a stirring speed of 300 rpm. The ligand was injected in 30 consecutive 10 μL aliquots with a 120 s spacing between injections. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a single binding site model. The binding affinity (K), enthalpy (ΔH), and stoichiometry (n) were determined from the fit. The heat of dilution was measured by injecting the ligand into buffer and subtracted from the raw data.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. Representative ITC trace, measured using 26 and the bromodomain of PB1(5); 30 consecutive injections of PB1(5) into a solution of 26 in 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05 mM TCEP. Raw heats (left) and normalized injection heats with a nonlinear least-squares fit for a single binding site model (right) are shown.

50505743.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to His6-tagged human recombinant SMARCA2B bromodomain expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)-R3-pRARE2 cells by VP-ITC microcalorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal VP-ITC instrument (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The protein (SMARCA2B bromodomain, 100 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the ligand (compound 26, 1 mM) was loaded into the syringe. The buffer was 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05 mM TCEP, pH 7.5. The ligand was injected in 30 consecutive 2 μL injections with 120 s spacing. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA) with a single-site binding model. The binding affinity (K_D) was calculated from the binding isotherm. The heat of dilution was determined by injecting the ligand into buffer alone and subtracted from the raw data.

Raw heats (left) and normalized injection heats with a nonlinear least-squares fit for a single binding site model (right) are shown.

50505740.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to His6-tagged human recombinant SMARCA4 bromodomain expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)-R3-pRARE2 cells by VP-ITC microcalorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal VP-ITC (Malvern Instruments) at 25 °C. The SMARCA4 bromodomain (100 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the compound (1–2 mM) was loaded into the syringe. The sample cell was filled with 1.4 mL of buffer (20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05 mM TCEP, pH 7.5). The compound was injected in 20 consecutive 2 μL injections with 120 s spacing. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a single-site binding model. The binding affinity (K_D) was calculated from the binding isotherm. The heat of dilution was determined by injecting the compound into buffer alone and subtracted from the raw data. The experiments were performed in triplicate, and the average K_D values are reported with standard deviations.
